replication.target_description: Unresolved: exposure-by-moral-belief interaction versus exposure simple effects under high and low moral belief; outcome unspecified.

notes: Identity assessed independently from supplied text: published 2023 Collabra: Psychology primary replication report, same full title as supplied OSF reference, authors Zhang, Cheung, Wong, Yuen, Sin, Chow, Feldman; DOI 10.1525/collabra.77610. Author names/order and year differ from supplied 2022 Yee et al. OSF reference, but the report explicitly identifies https://osf.io/j3ue4/ as its materials/data/code project. Accepted as the published version of that project with this discrepancy recorded. Text includes full report and supplementary material; no PDF supplied. Unassigned fields and original side are placeholders only. Candidates on p.11: shame exposure-by-moral-belief interaction F(2,1266)=15.90, p<.001, partial eta-squared .02; exposure simple effects under high moral belief F(2,629)=17.91, p<.001, partial eta-squared .05 and low moral belief F(2,637)=80.31, p<.001, partial eta-squared .20. Guilt has analogous tests and the mixed emotion model also includes exposure-by-moral-belief interaction. Description does not identify which test/outcome. Full-model N=1272 is a candidate only; simple-effect sample counts are not inferred from df.
